title: Research: Why does daemon mode crash frequently?
description:

Branch under investigation: customise/tldr-code (https://github.com/udhaya10/tldr-code/tree/customise/tldr-code)

- Collect daemon stderr/log + stats.jsonl + system signals at crash time
- Identify panic site(s) via backtraces or core dumps
- Classify crashes: panic vs OOM vs deadlock vs IPC drop vs OS signal
- Cross-reference with recent changes on customise/tldr-code branch
- File one bug-type bead per distinct root cause (linked via discovered-from)
- Summarise findings + recommended fixes

title: Research: Integrate cloud embedding models (e.g. Qwen3-Embedding-8B) into tldr semantic search
description:
tldr currently embeds locally via fastembed (snowflake-arctic-embed-m). Goal: design and prototype an integration path for cloud / API-based embedding providers, with Qwen3-Embedding-8B as the first target (also Voyage, OpenAI text-embedding-3, Cohere, etc.).

Driver: cloud models offer higher recall/precision and larger context, but introduce cost, latency, rate-limits, retries, secrets, and offline-mode trade-offs. Need a clear plug-point.

Related work already done:
- OpenContext CLI (oc) already abstracts EMBEDDING_API_KEY / EMBEDDING_API_BASE / EMBEDDING_MODEL — same shape we likely want
- Recent fork commit 285b0dc replaced bge-large-en-v1.5 with snowflake-arctic-embed-m, so the local-model swap path exists
acceptance_criteria:
- Map current embedding codepath in tldr-core (fastembed loader, vector store write, query embed)
- Identify the smallest seam to inject an alternate provider (trait/interface vs config-only)
- Provider API survey: Qwen3-Embedding-8B (DashScope), OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, Voyage voyage-3, Cohere embed-v3 — dimensions, max tokens, rate limits, pricing, batch size
- Decide config surface: env vars (EMBEDDING_API_KEY/BASE/MODEL like oc) vs config file vs both
- Design retry / backoff / timeout policy + offline fallback
- Vector-store compatibility: handle dimension mismatch on provider swap (re-index trigger)
- Secrets handling: where keys live, never logged, masked in stats
- Prototype: pluggable provider with at least one cloud backend (Qwen or OpenAI) behind a feature flag
- Benchmark: recall@k + latency vs current local model on a fixture corpus
- Document in docs/EMBEDDINGS.md (or thoughts/) including cost model

title: Research: Configuration file support appears partially implemented
description:
Attempts to configure tldr via a project / user configuration file did not work end-to-end. The codepath looks half-wired: some surfaces accept config (e.g. .tldrignore, env vars) but a unified tldr config file (yaml/toml/json) does not appear to be honoured consistently, suggesting the feature was started and abandoned.

Goal: trace what config mechanisms exist today, identify what was started-but-not-finished, and decide whether to (a) finish it, (b) document the actual supported config surface, or (c) cleanly remove the dead scaffolding.
acceptance_criteria:
- Catalogue every config input tldr currently reads: env vars, .tldrignore, .tldr/ dir, any *.toml/yaml/json
- Locate the parser / loader code for each (file paths + line refs)
- Identify dead-end paths: code that reads config keys that nothing else consumes, or vice versa
- Reproduce the failure: minimal config file + command that should react to it but doesn't
- Decide forward path with rationale: finish / document / remove
- File follow-up bug or feature beads for chosen path

title: Bug: 'tldr structure' auto-detection silently ignores minority languages
description:
When running 'tldr structure src/' without an explicit -l flag, auto-detection picks only the dominant language in the directory and silently skips all other source files. Users expect either: (a) per-file detection so every supported language is analysed, or (b) a clear warning that other languages were ignored.

Observed: a polyglot src/ produces structure output only for the language with the most files.
Expected: all supported languages in src/ are analysed, OR a visible message explains why some files were skipped.

Source line: docs/SETUP.md lines 60-64
  # Auto-detected
  tldr structure src/   # Detects from .py, .rs, .go, etc.

Reference branch: customise/tldr-code
acceptance_criteria:
- Reproduce in a polyglot dir (e.g., py + rs + go) and capture the silent skip
- Confirm whether this affects only 'structure' or other commands (calls, dead, search, etc.)
- Locate the auto-detect codepath (likely a single dominant-language picker)
- Decide policy: per-file multi-language vs explicit warning vs --languages flag
- Implement chosen fix
- Update docs/SETUP.md to describe actual behaviour
- Add a regression test on a multi-language fixture

title: Document tldr lifecycle failure modes missing from docs/SETUP.md
description:

Gaps observed:
- No description of panic / crash recovery
- No guidance on stale Unix socket cleanup after abnormal exit
- No mention of .tldr/ lock-file lifecycle
- No statement on what happens to in-flight requests when the daemon dies
- No documented log location for post-mortem analysis

title: Research: Understand how the tldr daemon works
description: Build a complete mental model of the tldr daemon: process lifecycle, IPC protocol, routing, request handling, and shutdown. Goal is to enable confident customisation downstream.
acceptance_criteria:
- Daemon start/stop/reconnect flow documented
- IPC transport + message format identified
- Request routing path from CLI to daemon to handler traced
- Concurrency model (threads/tasks/locks) understood
- Failure modes and recovery paths catalogued
- Findings captured in thoughts/ or docs/ as reference
notes: Search cache/callgraph experiments: Tested warm daemon and restarted/no-warm daemon. Result: cache warmth is NOT the key factor. Full-repo search without callgraph is consistently fast (~0.79s) both after warm and after daemon restart. Full-repo search with callgraph times out at 90s both after warm and after daemon restart, with zero output/stderr and daemon healthy/unchanged. Subdir search with callgraph (`crates/tldr-cli/src`, rust, 166 files) completes but takes ~49.5s and emits slow search log: `search completed in 49518ms ... callgraph=true`. Daemon salsa stats do not change during search, proving search is client-side and not using daemon warm cache. Assessment backed by experiments: the problem is not cold cache; it is live callgraph enrichment in `tldr search` rebuilding/processing callgraph client-side. Workaround: `--no-callgraph`. Fix: make search use cached/warmed callgraph or default to no-callgraph for large roots.

title: Research: Explore tldr output formats and design integration strategy
description:
tldr exposes five output formats: json (default), text, compact, sarif, dot. Each unlocks a different integration surface. Goal: try every format on real commands, document strengths/limits, and design a concrete integration plan for each.

Formats to cover:
  --format json      # structured, machine-readable
  --format text      # human-readable
  --format compact   # minified JSON for piping
  --format sarif     # GitHub Code Scanning / VS Code
  --format dot       # Graphviz visualisation
acceptance_criteria:
- For each format: run on at least 3 representative commands (e.g. structure, calls, smells, vuln, dead) and capture sample output
- Document: schema stability, field coverage, size, parse cost, downstream consumers
- json: design programmatic integration (TS/Py client lib? MCP tool exposure?)
- text: identify terminal-UX gaps (colour, paging, truncation)
- compact: pick canonical use cases (xargs/jq pipelines, log aggregation)
- sarif: GitHub Actions workflow + VS Code SARIF viewer wiring documented
- dot: Graphviz pipeline (svg/png) + interactive viewer (d3/cytoscape?) sketched
- Output: single design doc (thoughts/output-formats-integration.md) with one section per format and a prioritised integration roadmap
